description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $40,638.00 via TRACK Labor from Danos for multiple Materials Management and Supply Chain Specialists according to the attached JADE lines. These roles are not directly chargeable to the Joint Account under the Europa UOA as they are procurement related roles. Also, per COPAS MFI-21 Overhead Principles, purchasing is considered Overhead Indirect Costs and is not allowed to be billed as Direct Costs.

Indirect Costs are those costs not allowed to be billed as Direct Costs. These types of costs do not fit into one of the Direct Cost sections and are generally, but not necessarily, incurred off the Joint Property or above the Lease Level.

Examples of Indirect Costs are as follows:

Administration

Accounting Accounts payable Accounts receivable Office services Data processing Human resources Internal auditing Vendor audits

Operations Support Planning and follow-up Design and drafting (except when allowed as a direct charge, e.g., under Major Construction, Option B)

Inventory taking
classification_rationale: The disputed charges are for contract labor (Materials Management and Supply Chain Specialists billed via TRACK Labor from Danos) that the auditor argues are indirect/overhead costs not directly chargeable to the Joint Account.

description:

Josh Mills is a 3-dimensional modeler & coordinator plus laser scan survey organizer & director.

The 3D model is key not only to major maintenance & projects work execution but is a critical part of the Safety and Environmental Management System (SEMS) Mechanical Integrity. Mechanical Integrity §250.1916 Any work associated with inspections, inspection programs, LOD's of programs, AIPSM and MTO meetings (Assurance of Quality and Mechanical Integrity of Equipment).

Per the February 2019 Letter Agreement, a Technical Employee must have "...special and specific engineering, geological, geophysical, technical or operational skills...". This definition does not include design, drafting, or modeling skills which are considered overhead. As this modeler does not meet the definition of OTL due to not being a Technical Employee, his work is not chargeable under Section 3.1., 3.2., or 3.3. of the February Letter Agreement.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $143,398.10 plus OH of $9,132.80 for a total credit of $152,530.90.

- Michael Crochet-- Lead Wellsite Supervisor (Organization: Platform Well Interventions)-- Mr. Crochet was not found on the POB for the time that he was charged to the Joint Account.

The Operator claims that he was working on a "Project Study" and therefore was chargeable per the Agreed OTL Definitions and Billing Standards as agreed with the partners.

We noted that Mr. Crochet was working on A3 Wireline Intervention project and that this project has a 13% overhead and therefore was an Operating AFE and not associated with "field improvement or facility improvements or feasibility studies undertaken to progress future projects".

In its follow-up response, the Operator contends:

Well interventions are crucial for maintaining well productivity and ensuring efficient operation, used for various tasks such as milling, debris removal, plug setting, fishing, etc., staff coordinated for the intervention activities providing the inputs and activity descriptions. Hence has time written to the A3 well is deemed to be a project study.

Based on the above follow-up response, it is clear that the project was undertaken to maintain well productivity and ensure efficient operations. The work is not deemed to be field or facility improvement nor a feasibility study.

Thus, please credit the Joint account $6420.96 plus 64.781% burden and 13% overhead for a total of $11,955.99.
classification_rationale: The disputed charge is for direct staff labor (OTL) incorrectly charged to the Joint Account for an offsite technical staff member, making this a labor/payroll exception.

description:
The URSA Joint Account (O.US.REV.RC1.016.321277 and O.US.REV.RC1.016.324261) was allocated $601,584.28 from O.US.342.342.342.71300 of Allied Reliability TRACK report costs for the Audit Period. Total costs associated with Allied Reliability were $879,509.18 for the Audit Period with URSA receiving 68.4% of the costs.

Attached are the Allied Reliability TRACK Reports containing the personnel charged who were fulfilling the roles of GOM\_PS\_SE\_Work Prep Tech, GOM\_PS\_SE\_Maintenance Planner, and GOM\_PS\_SE\_ONS Discipline Planner. Of those, $421,623.87 were for offsite services. These offsite services are not chargeable in accordance with the Settlement Agreement, effective date December 19,2018, Exhibit C, Section 3.3 which states that to be directly chargeable to the joint account, scheduler(s), planners(s) and execution supporters must be working on "...facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities." The roles in question were working on general operations, per their charging WBS. Without supporting documentation evidencing that the roles are working specifically on facility maintenance, well maintenance and/or turnaround activities, these roles do not meet the definition of "Technical Employee" per Section 2 of the Agreement, and instead reverts to being an administrative function covered by overhead.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $288,390.73 ($421,623.87 * 68.4%), plus Operations Overhead at 13.0% ($37,490.79) , resulting in a total credit due of $325,881.52.

Related IR: IR051
classification_rationale: The disputed charges are for Allied Reliability personnel (planners, schedulers, execution supporters) whose labor costs were allocated to the joint account, and the exception argues these roles do not qualify as directly chargeable technical employees under the agreement.

description:
BP was charged a total of $544,698.23 net on its partner direct JADE. The backup attached to the journal entry shows that a total of $1,310,919 was charged to bp, XOM, and CoP in proportion to their working interests. It appears that this is a reclassification of 2021, 2022, and 2023 non-billable labor and its corresponding burden and overhead to billable labor/burden/overhead. However, the attached backup does not show which employees are being reclassified from nonbillable to billable. On IR-10, we requested the Operator to provide backup that identifies the employees being charged and how they benefitted the Joint Property.

In its response, the Operator provided a workbook showing the calculation of the partner direct charges. Per the Operator, these represent the billing out of unbilled staff costs related to the URSA Staff Home cost center (101045). The Operator also provided a list of staff who were tagged to URSA Staff home cost center on the same workbook.

We compared the list of employees provided on the workbook with direct labor charges and the PoB and noted the following (see notes on blue tabs on the file called "L&B workings 21-23 with EPS comments"):

- a. There are several employees who had already been charged as Direct Labor to the Joint Account.
- b. Several employees were only on the Joint Property during parts of the year and/or were on locations other than the Joint Property during parts of the year.
- c. A few employees were not found on the POB for the entire year.

Thus, we are unable to confirm that these partner direct charges relate to employees' work for the Joint Property.

We requested the Operator to provide details regarding which employees these partner direct charges are specifically for and for which time period so that we can ascertain that these charges benefitted Ursa. This follow-up request has not been fulfilled at the end of fieldwork.

Furthermore, we also requested the Operator to explain why its system of charging Labor over/under would not have already charged any employees' time which had not been timewritten. Per the description provided to us in the Audit Manual, it appears that if hours timewritten do not match actual hours worked or the tariff charged do not match the actual labor rate, then the system would have already automatically charged these out in Labor over/under, making a manual entry charging any unbilled labor costs unnecessary. We have not received an explanation for this query as of the end of fieldwork.
classification_rationale: The disputed charges are explicitly a reclassification of non-billable to billable labor costs (staff costs, burden, and overhead) for employees tied to the URSA Staff Home cost center, making this a labor exception.

description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $556,848.41 for EDG charges via the TRACK system per the attached JADE lines. Included in the charges are $545,672.79 for Cost Specialist(s), Document Controller, and Project Scheduler(s).

Project Schedulers are covered by overhead per the URSA JOA, Exhibit C, Section III "As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III (Overhead)....The cost and expense of services from outside sources in connection with matters of taxation, traffic, accounting or matters before or involving governmental agencies shall be considered as included in the overhead rates". Furthermore, these costs are not chargeable per the Settlement Agreement, effective date December 19,2018, Exhibit C, Section 2 which states that to be directly chargeable to the joint account, scheduler(s), planners (s) and execution supporters must be working on "...facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities". The Scheduler in question was working on major construction, development projects and general Opex, per the charging WBS codes. Absent of supporting documentation evidencing that the Scheduler was working specifically on a facility maintenance, well maintenance and/or turnaround activity, they do not meet the definition of "Technical Employee" per Section 2 of the Agreement, and instead reverts to being an administrative function covered by overhead.

Cost Specialists and Document Controllers are accounting and administrative functions covered by overhead per the JOA, Exhibit C, Section III ""As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III (Overhead)....The cost and expense of services from outside sources in connection with matters of taxation, traffic, accounting or matters before or involving governmental agencies shall be considered as included in the overhead rates". The Settlement Agreement, effective date December 19, 2018, Exhibit C, Section 2 also states "Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision, ... Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with these functions."

The Operator is therefore requested to credit the joint Account $545,672.79 plus overhead of $12,295.41 for a total credit due of $557,968.20.
classification_rationale: The disputed charges are for personnel costs (Cost Specialists, Document Controllers, and Project Schedulers) billed through the TRACK system that the auditor argues are administrative/overhead functions not directly chargeable to the joint account under the JOA.

description:
The Operator charged WBS C.US.WHL.PD.21.004.1230A (Project Leadership) $40,950.00 for SIEP time-writing of employee Theresa A Parkin (Emp# 215046) between June 2022 and December 2022.

The Deepwater Accounting Procedure attached to the governing Unit Operating Agreement effective January 1, 2016 - Section II.2.A(1) ( Labor - Feasibility Team and Integrated Project Team ) - directs the reader to Section II.7 ( Affiliate Services ). Section II.7.A.iii ( Affiliate Costs Associated with a Project ) states that 'charges for services of any Affiliate employees and contract services of the Affiliate engaged in activities or operations under the Agreement, provided the Affiliate employee or contractor is not performing functions covered by Section III ( Overhead ).' Section III ( Overhead ) specifically lists administration as covered by the overhead rate.

Given that the consolidated staff listing provided listed Ms. Parkin's job title during this period as 'Associate Business Admin Support' and she was not listed on the IPT provided for the period, her time is administrative costs covered by the overhead rate.

The Operator is requested to credit the Whale Joint Account $42,588.00 ($40,950.00 plus 4% overhead of $1,638.00) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

- Burden is higher due to the higher time writing for the month.

- Sevigny, Duane Francis
- David, Brad J
- Albritton, Adam
- The Operator's response regarding the burden does not make sense. Higher timewriting should not result in a higher burden rate. It appears that the rate being charged is around 86% {calculated as burden of ($194,947.21+62,982.94) divided by staff cost of $299,918.78} while the burden rate used for staff costs for 2024 should be 72.65%, resulting in a difference of $40,039. 168 hours X 3 employees x rate of $100.60 per hour ($299,918.78/2,981.30 hours) X 1.86 (burden rate charged) x 77.14% (percentage allocated to Joint Account)= $72,748.00.

(see tab "Location not URSA--IR 32b" -- their locations are noted in column AH of the tab). Please explain why these individuals were allocated to the Joint Account when they were located in other sites which were not URSA).

The Operator provided us with a workbook showing that these employees were either working onshore on regulatory projects or are offshore employees who were on vacation or training during the time charged. We have verified these and accept the Operator's response except for the following:

- William Ward-- Maintenance Team Lead. Mr. Ward charged 1,207.80 hours/ $154,755.08 (gross value=allocated value, ie 100% allocated to URSA), to the Joint Account. Please provide more details as to the type of work rendered by Mr. Ward and explain why his work is chargeable per the UOA and the 2018 settlement agreement.

Otherwise, credit the Joint Account $154,755.08 plus 13% overhead.
classification_rationale: The disputed charge is for labor hours and payroll costs of specific individuals (including a Maintenance Team Lead) allocated to the Joint Account, which is squarely a labor/personnel billing exception.

description:
The Joint Account was charged with $607,908.43 of direct labor for individuals who were not working on the Joint Account for the time in which they were charged, per the attached JADE lines. Their onsite locations during the time for which they charged the Joint Account are shown on column BF on the tab called "JADE lines." On a separate tab called "POB locations", we attach the documentation from the POB supporting our claim.

Please explain why these individuals were charged to the Joint Account when they were onsite another property; or credit the Joint Account $607,908.43 plus burden and overhead for a total of $1,060,319.13.

In its response, the Operator provided a workbook and noted: " we have conducted a comparison of the total monthly hours, calculated at 8 hours per day, against the hours spent at the other location. Any discrepancies or excess hours have been reviewed, and we are accepting any overcharged hours accordingly. " Based on this calculation, the Operator granted $ 67,636.92 of credits BEFORE burden and overhead.

We examined the logic of their calculations and do not agree that the credit granted is adequate. For example, taking the first person on the list: Michael Ables-- The POB shows he was at VITO whenever he is shown on the POB (snippet below).

The Operator explains their calculation of the credit (as related to January 2024 charges) for Michael Ables as such:

Ables, Michael

Based on POB, Michael was assigned to VITO from 01/10/2024 13:53 CST to 01/26/2024 13:12 CST, accounting for 17 days in January. This leaves 14 days available for allocation across other assets, including URSA. However, the total hours charged to URSA for January stand at 210 hours, which equates to approximately 26 days (assuming 8 hours/day). This results in an overlap of 12 days (~98 hours) beyond the available allocation. Accordingly, a credit of 98 hours is acknowledged and accepted for URSA. (Note by auditor-- actual credit granted was only 42 hours since the calculations used a 12 hour day instead of an 8 hour day.-- but we understand the logic being presented).

The operator does not assert that all periods during which staff were not in any specific platform are charged to URSA. The personnel in question belong to a shared resource pool, primarily from the MTAC (Maintenance, Turnaround, and Constructions) team. This team operates on a flexible assignment model, wherein staff are allocated to various projects based on operational requirements. When assigned to a specific project, their costs are directly charged to that project.

For activities supporting multiple assets, time is allocated based on individual timesheets submitted by the staff. The MTAC group records time against orders that reference CFR codes in the description field, as reflected in the Posting Object WBS/CC/OR field within JADE. These CFR codes fall under the scope of the OTA agreements.

The process of rationalizing overlapping hours is undertaken to identify the time spent on specific platforms or locations. This ensures that such time is directly charged to the respective location, rather than being distributed according to generalized percentage allocations provided by the teams.

This methodology is not flawed; rather, it represents a fair and logical approach to distinguishing total time from time spent on individual locations, in alignment with the POB.

It is incorrect to assume that any of the 210 hours charged for Michael Ables benefitted Ursa as that assumes that when he was not at VITO, that he would be working on URSA, as the calculation provided by the Operator implies. For the time charged in January or March, he was either on VITO, thus erroneously charged; or he was not onsite, thus, the Operator should explain why he is chargeable in accordance with the UOA or the 2018 letter agreement. The Operator noted in its response above that ' The MTAC group records time against orders that reference CFR codes in the description field, as reflected in the Posting Object WBS/CC/OR field within JADE. These CFR codes fall under the scope of the OTA agreements." However, an examination of the JADE lines show that there were not CFR references shown on the column Posting Object WBS/CC/OR. Furthermore, even if the group was supporting multiple assets, it appears that Mr. Ables was supporting Vito throughout the year. Thus, it is unlikely that an allocation of 14 days of his time ((210 hours less 42 hours credit granted)/12 hours per day) in January to URSA is "equitable" given that there was no evidence that he worked on URSA at all.

In its response, the Operator also provided a second example:

Bergeron, Bryan-- January charges

Bryan was assigned to MARS from 01/31/2024 08:51 CST to 02/14/2024 09:08 CST, which includes only 1 day in January. The remaining 30 days were available for allocation across multiple assets. In this case, 40 hours (5 days) were charged to URSA, which falls well within the available allocation.

Therefore, no credit is due for Bryan's January URSA charges.

This approach has been uniformly applied across all staff to identify overlapping days and validate URSA charges. It provides an unambiguous and efficient alternative to manually reviewing extensive timesheet entries, ensuring credibility and fairness in determining overcharged hours.

Again, we take issue with the logic of the calculation. The Joint Account was charged 40 hours but there is no evidence that Mr. Bergeron was working onsite the Joint Property. Thus, the Operator needs to either provide explanation as to what offsite work the employee is doing or credit the Joint Account. Simply implying that there are enough hours left in a particular month where the employee "may be working on URSA" is not enough evidence for chargeability.

In conclusion, we again assert that the employees brought forth here were not found onsite the Joint Property during the periods for which they were charged. Thus, we request the Operator to explain what work they were performing, how the work benefitted the Joint Property and if performed offsite, how their work is chargeable based on the provisions of the UOA or the 2018 Settlement Agreement.

While the Operator has already granted $ 67,636.92 BEFORE burden and overhead, unless the questions above are answered, we request a full credit of $1,060,319.13 ($607,908.43 plus burden and overhead, as calculated on JADE lines tab).
classification_rationale: The disputed charges are entirely about direct labor costs for named personnel whose timesheets were written to the wrong location/joint account, making this a labor/timesheet exception.

description:
The Operator charged the Whale Joint Account $52,243,329.87 for 2024 SIEP Affiliate Labor costs.

According to the Whale UOA Exhibit "C", Section II.7.A (Affiliate Costs Associated with a Project), the Operator may charge affiliate costs at a Cost Basis as "charged by the Affiliate to the Party providing such Affiliate services." Section I.5.C (Expenditure Audits) also states that "If Affiliate charges are billed using the Cost Basis, upon request from another Party, the Party providing an Affiliate will provide an annual report from a nationally recognized independent public accounting firm attesting that the charges billed from such Affiliate represent a complete and accurate allocation of its costs, and exclude any element of profit."

During the audit, the Operator was not able to provide the third-party report to substantiate the rates charged were valid and permissible.

The Operator is requested to provide the required supporting documentation or credit the Whale Joint Account $54,333,063.06 ($52,243,329.87 plus 4% overhead $2,089,733.19) with reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.
classification_rationale: The disputed charge is for SIEP Affiliate Labor costs billed to the joint account, which falls squarely within the Labor category covering affiliate charges and intercompany labor billing.
